editorial_intro: This week brings an exciting mix of new Indian content across various genres, including romantic dramas, action comedies, and gripping thrillers. Notable titles like 'Love Always' and 'Gajab Raat' are trending, making it a perfect time to refresh your watchlist.

picks.title: Love Always
picks.synopsis: A long-married couple, Kannan and Manjula, whose relationship has reached a breaking point, are magically given the chance to revisit their youth — reliving their romance as their younger selves while their present-day marriage is tested. It is the first Tamil adaptation of the Korean webtoon 'Here We Go Again'.
picks.why_watch: A warm, quirky age-reversal romance — the first Korean-webtoon adaptation in Tamil streaming — with Jayasudha and Jayaprakash as the older couple and Gouri Kishan and Ramzan Muhammed as their younger selves.

picks.title: Gajab Raat
picks.synopsis: Set over a single night in Delhi, corrupt sub-inspector Ajay Nirvit (Manoj Bajpayee) is assigned the case of a young journalist found brutally injured after being thrown from a moving car at Connaught Place. As officers from the CBI and NIA circle the case, he uncovers a conspiracy linking a powerful politician and pharmaceutical companies to a manufactured vaccine shortage.
picks.why_watch: Ritesh Shah's directorial debut, written and produced by Neeraj Pandey — a tense one-night thriller that hit No. 1 on Netflix India's Top 10.

picks.title: Chaar Yaar
picks.synopsis: Set in early-2000s Mumbai, four friends from modest backgrounds — Jay, Tony, Saahil and Sameer — turn to stealing luxury cars to escape their financial struggles. One decision pulls them into a dangerous world of gangsters and a relentless police pursuit that tests their friendship.
picks.why_watch: A gritty, Satya-style crime saga told through a young cast — eight episodes of friendship, ambition and bad decisions in millennium-era Mumbai.

picks.title: Pooja Meri Jaan
picks.synopsis: Pooja Dogra's rejection of her close friend Aniket's romantic advances ends in tragedy when he dies by suicide — and Pooja is arrested for abetment. Corporate lawyer Sana takes up her defence in a courtroom fight over obsession, rejection and consent.
picks.why_watch: A sobering thriller about stalking and consent, anchored by Mrunal Thakur and Huma Qureshi — far darker than its title suggests.

picks.title: Ashakal Aayiram
picks.synopsis: Ajeesh Hariharan, a carefree youngster who dreams of stardom as his social-media persona 'Junior Prince', sees his ordinary life upended when a superstar's film shoot arrives in his neighbourhood — and his bond with his father Hariharan is tested and rebuilt along the way.
picks.why_watch: Real-life father and son Jayaram and Kalidas Jayaram share the screen in this warm Malayalam family comedy-drama, reuniting as leads more than two decades after Ente Veedu Appuvinteyum.

picks.title: The Terminal List: Season 2
picks.synopsis: Adapting Jack Carr's novel 'True Believer', Season 2 picks up months after James Reece finished his list: offered a pardon if he hunts down a terrorist he once trained, Reece is pulled back into a globetrotting mission alongside Raife Hastings.
picks.why_watch: With intense action sequences and a gripping storyline, this series keeps you on the edge of your seat while exploring themes of loyalty and revenge.
